# UX.md — [Business]

What a new designer or writer on this project would need to be told. Read
with CLAUDE.md (the brief) and DESIGN.md (the tokens). Keep it current;
a stale UX.md is applied with full confidence.

## Who the users are
[Two or three user models from real research. For each: goals, constraints,
decision triggers, and the evidence that supports each claim. No invented
names, no stock traits.]

## What they are trying to do
[The top three jobs, in the users' own words where you have them.]

## What we know
[Research findings, dated and sourced. Interview themes with quote counts.
Support-ticket patterns. Analytics facts. Usability-test findings by severity.]

## Interaction standards
[The rules that recur. Examples:]
- One primary action per screen.
- Forms show errors inline, next to the field, after the person leaves it.
- Destructive actions confirm with the action's name on the button.
- Loading states name what is loading.
- Empty states offer one action.

## Terminology
[Term the product uses → terms to avoid. Example: "booking", not "reservation" or "appointment".]

## Domain rules
[Facts about the business an outsider would get wrong: opening hours logic,
pricing rules, legal wording that must appear, things that must never be
promised.]

## Known constraints
[Technical, legal, brand or client constraints that shape every decision.]
